about: Field of view / detection parameters per unit type for timeline mode. sweepWidthM = effective sweep width W (Koopman): per searcher / per sensor, daytime, unresponsive subject, rested crew. Coverage of a 100 m cell: C = W * trackLengthInCell / cellArea; POD = 1 - exp(-C). Values are conservative; every value marked est is an estimate (no direct published number). Not TOPR/GOPR/WOPR operating rules.

terrainClassMap.forestOverlay: forest (ProbabilityGrid.forest[cell] == true replaces the class value for land classes, except water)

pod.formula: POD = 1 - exp(-C), C = sum over minutes of W_eff * trackM / cellAreaM2
pod.combine: cumulative POD over units and minutes: 1 - exp(-sum C) (equivalent to 1 - prod(1 - POD_i))

ground.notes: Per searcher. A line of n searchers = n tracks. Day ESW for a medium-visibility adult in temperate forest 64 m, night 22 m (Cf 0.34), weak lights <200 lux another x0.5. Published range 17 m (dense forest, low-vis adult) to 142 m (open winter hardwood, high-vis adult). Forest chosen below 64 m because Polish mountain forest is leaf-on spruce with understorey. dwarfPine, scree, slab, cliff, water are est. A responsive subject (answers calls / whistle) adds an auditory W of about 300 m (NZ mountain experiment 306-460 m); the visual table assumes unresponsive.

windCone.direction: cone opens UPWIND from the dog (the dog smells sources upwind of it; the scent plume itself drifts downwind from the subject)

rangeM.note: calm: no direction, small circle; convection lifts scent at midday
strong wind dilutes and shears the plume

windCone.mountainThermals: day (sun on slope): air flows upslope, cone points downslope/below the dog is less useful, search along ridges and downhill; evening/night: katabatic downslope flow, work up gullies from below

dog.notes: Air-scent dog team, area search. Mean ESW of 4 teams 95 m (95% CI 44-145 m). Handbook: dog POD 5-95% at 100 m spacing depending on weather; night and morning/evening better than calm sunny midday (convection). Greatbatch 2015 found no correlation of wind/temperature with effectiveness, so wind cone values are est. Trailing dogs follow a track (width ~10-30 m around the track) and are not modeled as area cover. Water: dog only on shore / from boat, est. Terrain values below 95 m are est.

drone.notes: Nadir thermal camera at 80 m AGL. Footprint = 2 * AGL * tan(HFOV/2). W chosen at about 0.8 of footprint width in the open (operator watches live video; misses are common), lower in clutter. Max AGL where a 0.5 m body is 1.5 px (Johnson detection) is about 250 m, but a human watching video needs 4+ px, so 80-100 m AGL. Single thermal frames under dense canopy rarely show a person (Bimber AOS: practical only with multi-view integration), so forest W is est at 0.2 of open. Sun-warmed scree/slab in daytime x0.8 (already in the engine). Night better thermal contrast x1.1. Engine currently uses widthM 120: about 2x this value.

heli.notes: Visual search from helicopter at 300-500 ft. Water: USCG/IAMSAR person in water 0.1 NM (185 m) for 300-500 ft, all visibilities; x4 with lifejacket (PFD) up to 500 ft. Land: no open-access table found; open 300 m is est, scaled by IAMSAR terrain/vegetation factors (0.5 for 15-60% vegetation or hilly, 0.3 for 60-85% or mountainous, 0.1 above 85%). Night: NVG unilluminated PIW without PFD 0.01 NM vs 0.1 NM by day (x0.1); with FLIR turret est x0.5. Engine gates: no flight under 500 m visibility, wind > 18 m/s.

boat.notes: Small boat SRU, person in water: USCG table 0.2 NM (370 m) at 1-3 NM visibility, 0.3 NM (555 m) at 5+ NM. Chosen 300 m: lake chop, untrained crew, head-only target. Land classes: shoreline scan from the water only, est. Night: unlit PIW nearly impossible to see without light; searchlight est 0.3. PFD factor 2 is est (USCG x4 is for aircraft).

diver.sweepWidthFromVisibility: W = min(2 * visibilityM, 6); zero visibility: tactile search W 1.5 m (arm reach on a jackstay line)
diver.notes: Underwater visibility in Polish lakes: Secchi depth below 1 m turbid, 2-4 m good, record 10-12 m (Powidzkie, Hancza). Horizontal visibility taken ~ Secchi depth (est). Underwater light is artificial anyway, so nightFactor 1 for detection; the engine gates divers at night for safety. Engine widthM 15 is about 5x too wide.

lineOfSight.dem: Ray from observer (ground elevation + observerHeightM) to target cell centre + 0.3 m (lying person); blocked if any DEM sample in between is above the ray. Sample every 25 m. Cells beyond maxRangeM are not covered.
lineOfSight.forest: Visual: each 100 m of forest along the ray multiplies visibility by forestLosAttenuationPer100m (ground 0.1). Aerial thermal: target cell in forest multiplies W by forestThermalPassThrough (no attenuation along the ray, looking down).
lineOfSight.dog: No LOS. Ridges still block scent: if the DEM ray from the dog to the cell crosses a ridge more than 20 m above both ends, set coverage to 0 (est).
